title: The Sixth Constable: The Magpie's Treasure
full_text:
The Sixth Constable addressed the Sultan: "Sire, a high-born lady of the court brought her young maidservant before me in chains, demanding she be whipped and imprisoned for the theft of an emerald necklace of immense value. The maiden knelt in the dust, weeping tears of agony and swearing by her honor and her ancestors that she had never touched her mistress's jewels, though none in the household would believe her."

"I accompanied the lady to her private bedchamber to investigate the scene. The room was tidy, but I noted that the arched window stood wide open, looking out into a high garden courtyard dominated by an ancient cedar tree. Upon a high fork in the branches, I spotted a nest belonging to a pair of wild magpies—birds famous across the world for their instinct to steal glittering objects."

"I sent an agile stable boy up the cedar branches to inspect the nest. There, woven between dry twigs and horsehair, lay the missing emerald necklace, alongside three silver sewing pins and a gilded button! The noble lady wept in bitter remorse, struck off the girl's fetters with her own hands, and bestowed upon her a dowry of two hundred dinars, learning that haste in condemnation brings lifelong shame."
moral: Do not accuse an innocent servant of theft before searching all natural possibilities.

quiz.question: What is the central moral lesson taught in "Sixth Constable's History"?
options: Presence of mind and quiet wisdom triumph over brute strength.
Acting in haste and anger without thinking
Believing rumors and flattery without proof
